title: Slow English Podcast #170: Papua New Guniea

sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily.
I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Papua New Guinea.
It is a country full of jungles, mountains,
and many cultures.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Papua New Guinea?
Papua New Guinea is in the Pacific Ocean,
in a region called Oceania.
It is on the island of New Guinea,
which it shares with Indonesia.
To the south is Australia, across the sea.
It has many islands, mountains, and rainforests.
What is the capital city of Papua New Guinea?
The capital city is Port Moresby.
It is on the southern coast of the country.
It has offices, markets, schools, and an airport.
Other towns include Lai,
a big port and industrial center,
Mount Hagan in the highlands,
Madang known for diving and beaches.
How many people live in Papua New Guinea?
About 9 million people live in Papua New Guinea.
Most people live in villages or small towns.
The country is known for its many cultures and languages.
What language do people speak?
Papua New Guinea has over 800 languages.
The main languages are
Top person, a Creole language,
widely spoken English,
used in schools and government.
Hiri Motu, spoken in the south.
Many people also speak local tribal languages in their villages.
What is the weather like in Papua New Guinea?
The weather is hot and wet.
It is tropical all year round.
Rainy season from December to March.
Dryer season from May to October.
There are many rivers, lakes, and humid forests.
What does Papua New Guinea look like?
It has tall mountains and volcanoes,
thick jungles and rainforests, rivers, lakes, and swamps.
Islands and coral reefs.
Much of the land is wild, green, and beautiful.
What animals live there?
Papua New Guinea is full of unique animals,
such as tree kangaroos,
birds of paradise,
colorful birds with long feathers,
cassowaries, large flightless birds,
bats, frogs, and insects.
Snakes and lizards.
In the sea, you can find fish, turtles, and coral.
What do people eat in Papua New Guinea?
Food is local, natural, and often cooked on a fire.
People eat tarot, sweet potatoes, and yams.
Bananas, pineapple, and coconut.
Chicken, fish, or pork.
Sago, a starch from a tree, used like porridge.
Popular foods.
Lumu, food cooked in the ground with hot stones,
boiled greens with coconut,
grilled fish with tarot or sweet potato.
What do people drink in Papua New Guinea?
People drink water, tea and instant coffee,
coconut water, fruit juice.
In rural areas, people may drink rainwater or water from well.
What is life like in Papua New Guinea?
Life is often rural, traditional, and community-based.
People enjoy farming, fishing, and hunting.
Building homes from wooden leaves,
telling stories, and singing songs.
Going to church, dancing and wearing traditional clothes at festivals.
Family and tribe are very important in daily life.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Independence Day, September 16, Christmas and Easter.
Cultural festivals with masks, drums, and traditional dances.
Sing-sings where different tribes perform music and dance,
weddings, and initiation ceremonies.
People paint their faces, wear feathers, and dance together.
Some fun facts about Papua New Guinea.
It has over 800 languages, more than any other country.
Many people live without roads or electricity.
It has rainforests that are millions of years old.
The National Flag has a bird of paradise and southern cross stars.
Many people still use traditional tools and farming.
Now you know many things about Papua New Guinea.
You know where it is, what people eat, and how they live.
You learned about the forests, animals, and culture.
Great job.
I am Emily.
Goodbye, or as they say and talk, peace and goodbye.
